title: Food & drink
goal: Order food and drinks, say what you want, what you like and don't like, and that you're hungry or thirsty.
intro:
Food is one of the great joys of learning Hindi — from roadside chai to a full thali. In this unit you'll learn the everyday foods and tastes, and how to order.

Grammatically, you'll meet a big idea: in Hindi, wanting, liking and feeling hungry are things that **happen to you**. Instead of 'I want tea', Hindi says 'to me, tea is needed' — **मुझे चाय चाहिए**.

vocab.note: Also used for smoking: सिगरेट पीना
f · usually brewed with milk, sugar and spices
m · cooked rice in the east is भात
m · also मांस māṃs (formal), and 'मीट', 'चिकन', 'मटन' from English
Formal-ish; in speech बढ़िया baṛhiyā, मज़ेदार mazedār or 'टेस्टी'
f · मुझे भूख लगी है 'I'm hungry'
Common in speech: 'veg'; non-vegetarian: मांसाहारी or 'non-veg'
Used with मुझे etc.: मुझे पानी चाहिए 'I need water'
Dative of मैं. Also मुझको mujhko.

phrases.en: What would you like? / What do you need?
Not too spicy, please. (lit. less chilli)
Have some more roti! (host to guest)
That's it, I'm full. (lit. stomach has filled)

grammar.title: 'To me' constructions: मुझे … चाहिए
grammar.body:
Many feelings and needs in Hindi are expressed with the person in the **dative** ('to me') and the thing as the grammatical subject. 'I want/need water' is **मुझे पानी चाहिए** — literally 'to me water is needed'. 'I'm hungry' is **मुझे भूख लगी है** — 'to me hunger has struck'.

The dative pronouns (you'll use them constantly):

मैं → **मुझे** (मुझको) — to me
तुम → **तुम्हें** (तुमको)
आप → **आपको**
वह → **उसे** (उसको); यह → **इसे** (इसको)
हम → **हमें** (हमको)
वे → **उन्हें** (उनको); ये → **इन्हें** (इनको)

With nouns and names use **को**: राम को, बच्चों को. **चाहिए** never changes for the person, so it's very easy: मुझे / आपको / उन्हें चाय चाहिए.

grammar.title: Liking: मुझे … पसंद है
grammar.body:
'I like X' follows the same pattern: **मुझे X पसंद है** — 'to me X is liked'. The verb agrees with the thing liked: है for one thing, **हैं** for several (मुझे आम पसंद हैं 'I like mangoes').

To say you like **doing** something, use the infinitive (the -ना form): मुझे खाना बनाना पसंद है 'I like cooking'.

For the experience of something tasting/seeming nice, Hindi uses **अच्छा लगना** 'to seem good': मुझे यह चाय अच्छी लगी 'I liked this tea'. And the negative is simply नहीं: मुझे मछली पसंद नहीं है.

examples.native: हमें दाल बहुत अच्छी लगती है।
examples.roman: hameṃ dāl bahut achchhī lagtī hai.

dialogue.title: Lunch at a dhaba
dialogue.setting: Anna and her colleague Vikram stop at a roadside restaurant (dhaba) on the highway.

lines.speaker: Vikram
lines.native: मुझे बहुत भूख लगी है। दाल, रोटी और आलू की सब्ज़ी।
lines.roman: mujhe bahut bhūkh lagī hai. dāl, roṭī aur ālū kī sabzī.
lines.en: I'm very hungry. Dal, roti and potato curry.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.native: मैं शाकाहारी हूँ। मुझे भी दाल और चावल चाहिए। कम मिर्च, प्लीज़।
lines.roman: maiṃ shākāhārī hūṃ. mujhe bhī dāl aur chāval chāhiye. kam mirch, plīz.
lines.en: I'm vegetarian. I'd also like dal and rice. Not too spicy, please.

lines.speaker: Vikram
lines.native: दो चाय और एक गिलास पानी।
lines.roman: do chāy aur ek gilās pānī.
lines.en: Two teas and a glass of water.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.native: मेरी चाय बिना चीनी की, प्लीज़।
lines.roman: merī chāy binā chīnī kī, plīz.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.native: बहुत स्वादिष्ट है! मुझे यह दाल बहुत पसंद है।
lines.roman: bahut svādiṣṭ hai! mujhe yah dāl bahut pasand hai.
lines.en: It's delicious! I really like this dal.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.native: नहीं, बस, पेट भर गया। भैया, बिल लाइए।
lines.roman: nahīṃ, bas, peṭ bhar gayā. bhaiyā, bil lāiye.
lines.en: No, that's it, I'm full. Excuse me, the bill please.

culture: Hospitality runs deep: a host will offer more food again and again, and a single 'no' is often taken as politeness. Say **बस, पेट भर गया** with a hand over your plate. Many Indians are vegetarian, and restaurants often label food **veg** (green dot) or **non-veg** (red/brown dot); some vegetarians also avoid eggs, onion or garlic. Eat with your **right hand**. Chai is offered everywhere — in homes, shops and offices — and accepting a cup is a friendly gesture.

tip.title: मुझे … चाहिए — I'd like / I need
tip.body:
- Hindi says 'to me tea is needed': **मुझे** चाय **चाहिए**.
- The person takes the 'to' form: मुझे, **आपको**, **तुम्हें**, **उसे**, **हमें**; with nouns add **को**: बच्चों को.
- **चाहिए** never changes. The trap: never मैं चाय चाहिए.

sentences.native: मुझे चाय नहीं चाहिए, कॉफ़ी चाहिए।
sentences.roman: mujhe chāy nahīṃ chāhiye, kofī chāhiye.
sentences.en: I don't want tea, I want coffee.

tip.title: Hunger 'strikes' you
tip.body:
- 'I'm hungry' = **मुझे भूख लगी है** (lit. 'to me hunger has struck'); thirsty: **मुझे प्यास लगी है**.
- Same 'to me' form as चाहिए: आपको, उसे, बच्चों को.
- **खाना** is both 'food' and 'to eat'; **पीना** 'to drink': मैं चाय पीता हूँ.

sentences.native: मुझे दो रोटी और दाल चाहिए।
sentences.roman: mujhe do roṭī aur dāl chāhiye.
sentences.en: I'd like two rotis and dal.

sentences.native: आलू की सब्ज़ी बहुत अच्छी है।
sentences.roman: ālū kī sabzī bahut achchhī hai.
sentences.en: The potato curry is really good.
I don't want roti, I want rice.

tip.title: Tastes agree with the dish
tip.body:
- Taste words in **-ā** agree: दाल **तीखी** है (f), खाना **तीखा** है (m), चाय **मीठी** है.
- **कम मिर्च** 'less chilli' is the magic phrase if you can't take heat.
- **बिना** … **की/का** 'without': बिना चीनी **की** चाय (चाय is f).

sentences.en: The curry is a little sweet.

sentences.native: मुझे बिना चीनी की कॉफ़ी चाहिए।
sentences.roman: mujhe binā chīnī kī kofī chāhiye.

sentences.en: Is there sugar in the tea?

lessons.title: What you like, and when you're full

tip.title: मुझे … पसंद है — I like
tip.body:
- 'I like X' = **मुझे X पसंद है** ('to me X is liked'), same 'to me' form as चाहिए.
- The verb follows the thing liked: **है** for one, **हैं** for several: मुझे अंडे पसंद **हैं**.
- A host says **लीजिए** 'have some'; you answer **बस** 'enough'.

sentences.native: मुझे भारतीय खाना बहुत पसंद है।
sentences.roman: mujhe bhārtīy khānā bahut pasand hai.

sentences.native: मुझे तीखा खाना पसंद नहीं है।
sentences.roman: mujhe tīkhā khānā pasand nahīṃ hai.

sentences.en: Could you bring some water, please?
